messages.content: "Can you tell me the scores for the Manchester United soccer team in the English Premier League for the last 5 rounds and also the scores for the Los Angeles Lakers basketball team in the NBA for the last 7 rounds?"

function.name: basketball_scores_get_scores
function.description: Retrieve basketball scores for a specific team and league within a certain range of rounds. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

team.description: The basketball team whose scores are to be retrieved.

league.description: The league in which the team competes.

rounds.description: Number of past rounds for which to retrieve the scores.

2) Basketball scores for LA Lakers (NBA) for last 7 rounds.

First we should call soccer API: team="Manchester United", league="English Premier League", rounds=5.

Second we call basketball API: team="Los Angeles Lakers", league="NBA", rounds=7.

We'll produce calls accordingly. We'll use the tool invocation format exactly as specified. Then after receiving results from both calls, we'll combine them into a single JSON object containing "manchester_united_soccer_results": [...], "los_angeles_lakers_basketball_results":[...] etc.

But note: According to instructions, we can only output one response at a time? Actually we can do multiple responses but they will be combined automatically if we provide all outputs. But we might want to first make the calls sequentially or concurrently. Let's just call soccer then basketball. After retrieving both, we return combined result.

Thus steps:

Call soccer_scores_get_scores(team="Manchester United", league="English Premier League", rounds=5).

Then call basketball_scores_get_scores(team="Los Angeles Lakers", league="NBA", rounds=7).

After getting both results, respond with combined JSON.

Let's proceed.
